https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/t.body: The United States Mid Term elections have come and gone. They have left an untidy rubble with an ill-mannered despotic president, a badly injured Republican party and badly damaged institutions of the American state. The ultimate outcome of a toppling of the Republican majority in Congress may be a salvaging of American democracy and the institutional framework of the nation. But if Trump remains in the White House, the threat to America’s democracy may persist as he resorts to endless vetoes to plough his way forward. At the worst, Donald Trump could be impeached and sent packing from the White House. At the best, his presidency could be tempered by the norms of democratic civility. The latter possibility, Trump will cease to be Trump. Less bluster. Fewer audacious lies. There may be less strategic blunders and playing with dangerous war planes, missiles and drones. Hopefully, there will now be greater respect for the rules based international order and more respect for the international community of nations and its leaders who have endured two years of Donald Trump’s unwarranted insults and habitual diplomatic bad manners. But the US constitution still leaves a sinking Trump with a desperate lifeline: the power to veto whatever Congress decides and he disagrees with. The impending relief is systemic. Just when both Americans and the wider world had lost hope in the survival of the show place of democracy, the American electorate hit the reverse button. The just concluded Mid Term elections into governorship and congressional seats has begun the reversal of the draining of Donald Trump’s Washington swamp. A president who initially swore he was out to drain the swamp in Washington became himself a personification of the swamp. He rode rough shod on Congress, exploiting his party’s congressional majority in both houses to literally run the United States more like an authoritarian Banana Republic. He tested the American judiciary by putting nearly all his authoritarian whims to judicial test. The Supreme Court just managed to retain a precarious integrity by reserving interim rulings on virtually everything from demolitions of sections of the White House to erect a controversial Ball Room or a laughable ‘reflective pool’. Even tangential ego driven skirmishes like renaming the Kennedy Centre and every street corner after himself became subjects of unrelenting litigations and contentious judicial pronouncements. Over and above his many domestic excesses, Donald Trump saw the rest of the world as an adolescent playing field to test his many illusions of power and illiterate readings of power, politics and international affairs. He invaded nations within reach, imposed silly tariffs on literally every nation in the world and talked down on virtually all respectable leaders. He spoke to and about the United Nations in condescending language unheard in its chambers since after its formation in 1945. And because of America’s considerable economic and military strategic prowess, most of the world looked on in consternation and awe as the great American democratic Olympus tottered and towered over all in unsightly apparel and unbecoming language. Matters would have been easier if the effect of Donald Trump’s wrecking ball autocracy was limited to the United States and its immediate neighbourhood. Not quite. Under the illusion of being thought strong but actually afraid of his own weakness, Trump launched a hazy war against Iran. Egged on by his cabinet of adolescent secretaries especially a certain infantile Pete Hegseth, Trump has in the last eight months hurled any number of missiles, bombs and drones at Iran with questionable impact except a pro-Zionist propaganda of conquest. Iran is of course far from being humiliated or defeated in any sense. Instead, US allies in the Middle East have all been dragged into a war they never prepared for or envisaged. Unlikely places like Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha, Aman, Riyadh and other previously peaceful places have become targets of Iran reprisal drone and rocket attacks. An entire region has been plunged into war at the behest of President Trump and his partner, Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, a man wanted abroad by the ICC for myriad human rights abuse crimes and at home for many corruption charges. Even far off places like Europe bore the brunt of Trump’s tactless foreign escapades. At home, President Trump is alleged to have exploited his office for corrupt ends. His family is known to pursue multiple business interests all around the world where the US has interests. The president has himself engaged in insider trading in companies that have business with the US government. Not to talk of multiple rackets in crypto currency and murky deals in Venezuelan oil. Donald Trump’s authoritarian inclinations and compulsive corruption would have paled into insignificance if the US domestic economy under his presidency enabled the ordinary American to enjoy an affordable normal life. On the contrary, the endless war with Iran has turned the strategic Strait of Hormuz into a death bed for ships of all nations and made oil cargo traffic a nightmare for strong and weak nations. Global oil process have since shot through the roof. Gasoline pump prices in America have shot up from a little over $2 before the war to more than $4 in the Mid Term week. Prices in grocery shops have taken a similar hike. In general, all those who voted for Donald Trump two years ago are all writhing under the pain of economic hardship. Therefore, the outcome of the Mid Terms was very predictable. That is the reality that has unfolded before our very eyes. All that was left to save the world from the Trumpian ultimate nightmare was a test of the democratic core of America through the Mid Terms. It was a historic test of the democratic state. The American voter was once again called upon to use the power of the ballot to tame the autocratic inclinations of the president through a revalidation of the mandate of members of Congress as representatives of the people. Here lies the import of the Mid Terms as an instrument for the revalidation of the popular will in America’s democracy. In the delicate balance between the individual leader and the institutions of the democratic state, Trump weighed too heavily as an elected leader. He literally overwhelmed the state and disorganized it. Congress, the judiciary, law enforcement, the federal bureaucracy, were all bent and twisted to conform to the wishes of an authoritarian “king” Trump. In the post Midterm reclamation period, there will be stresses and strains between the president and the institutions he has already mangled. The major one will be the clashes between the rescued institutions of state and the stubborn idiosyncratic tendencies of an authoritarian president. Trump will remain recalcitrant, belligerent, abusive, defiant of rules and inclined to lawlessness. Under the guise of applying the rules of business deal making, Try will try to flout the rules of diplomatic negotiation and structured engagement for his personal advantage and the benefit of his family, friends, associates and cronies. The remaining Trump tenure will remain a terrain dominated by the Elon Musks of this world. By way of a general backdrop, the thrashing of the Trump presidency in the just concluded Midterms is a consequence of the wider implications of Trump’s political misadventure and historic displacement. For over two centuries, it was a dream that attracted all from every corner of the world. The pull of America was in its diversity, the freedom of its society, its robust spirit of enterprise that made every one that lived in America a partaker in a legacy of prosperity in a free society. The American dream came to be a shared dream of everyone that was born in or moved to live in America. Simply put, the American dream boiled down to the right of everyone in America to join the race for the pursuit of happiness through hard work, focused aspiration and an entitlement to the fruits of honest labour. But under our very eyes, in our own life time, the American dream has turned into a nightmare. The land where everyone fled to as a last resort of freedom and safety has become an unwelcome hellhole. So called illegal immigrants are being hounded and chased around major American cities and shot on the streets in broad day light like mad dogs by untrained and bigoted immigration hounds. In the name of anti-immigration, innocent settlers some of whom have lived in America for upwards of 3-4 decades have been hounded down, loaded into war planes and deported to countries that they left many years ago without memories. The reign of Donald Trump as a second term President has witnessed the systematic erosion of everything that distinguished America as a civilizational force. It is now a dark force, a force of ill both at home and abroad. America under Trump has become an anti Islamic force but a Zionist champion, a bigoted white supremacist bastion. Its society is divided along racial, perception lines. The US Mid Terms may have come as a much needed check on authoritarian drifts of the system. The president now has to obtain the authority of a more diverse congress to engage in further flirtations. But the damage that Trump’s authoritarian flirtations have done to the world and the US system is considerable. He has waged wars without congressional approval. He has killed people in open seas without caring to prove that they committed any crimes. He has livid war against sovereign states without anyone’s approval but only his instincts. He has deployed aircraft carriers into the seas of the world, ordered precision bombings, allowed the deployment of advanced missiles systems and aircraft only by a phone call to his adolescent Secretary of War. The abiding question now is: how does the world recover from the vast damages done to America and the world in the wild days when democracy went unguarded under the rampaging assault of an unrepentant autocrat who was however elected by a democracy. An elaborate repair job stares America in the face with a menacing urgency. The guardrails of democratic civility need to be rebuilt. Washington needs to re-cultivate decent political manners and rhetoric. Above all, America needs to unlearn the kind of vulgarity in the presidency that elevates Mickey Minaj’s bum into a subject for a presidential public utterance. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/t.title_zh: 特朗普：失态举止的危险
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/08/t.body_zh: 美国中期选举已经结束，留下一片狼藉：一位态度无礼、专横跋扈的总统，一个伤势严重的共和党，以及遭到严重破坏的美国国家制度。共和党在国会中的多数地位被推翻，最终可能挽救美国的民主和这个国家的制度框架。然而，如果特朗普继续留在白宫，美国民主所面临的威胁仍可能持续，因为他会不断动用否决权，强行推进自己的主张。最坏的情况下，唐纳德·特朗普可能遭到弹劾，被逐出白宫；最好的情况下，他的总统任期将受到民主礼仪规范的约束。但若出现后一种情况，特朗普将不再是特朗普。他的虚张声势会减少，胆大妄为的谎言会减少，故意作出的战略失误以及拿危险战机、导弹和无人机玩乐的举动也可能减少。希望今后能够更加尊重以规则为基础的国际秩序，也更加尊重国际社会及其领导人；这些人和国家已经忍受了唐纳德·特朗普两年以来无端的侮辱和一贯恶劣的外交礼仪。然而，美国宪法仍给陷入困境的特朗普留下一根救命的绳索：无论国会作出何种决定，只要他不同意，他都拥有否决权。即将到来的缓解将是系统性的。就在美国人和世界其他地方都对这座民主橱窗能否存续失去希望之际，美国选民按下了倒退键。刚刚结束的州长和国会席位中期选举，已经开始扭转唐纳德·特朗普华盛顿沼泽不断恶化的局面。这位起初宣誓要清理华盛顿沼泽的总统，最终却成了沼泽的化身。他粗暴地凌驾于国会之上，利用本党在两院占据的国会多数，实际上把美国治理得更像一个独裁的香蕉共和国。他把自己几乎所有专横任性的念头都交由司法部门检验，借此试探美国司法系统。最高法院勉强维持了岌岌可危的完整性，对从拆除白宫部分区域，到修建颇具争议的宴会厅或荒唐的“倒影池”等 virtually 一切事务，均暂缓作出裁决。即使是给肯尼迪中心和每个街角重新命名这类由自我意识驱动的旁支冲突，也引发了无休止的诉讼和充满争议的司法裁决。除了众多国内失当行为之外，唐纳德·特朗普还把世界其他地方视为一个 adolescent playing field，用来检验他种种权力幻觉，以及他对权力、政治和国际事务不学无术的理解。他入侵力所能及的国家，对世界上几乎每个国家征收荒唐关税，还几乎对所有受人尊敬的领导人居高临下地说话。自联合国于1945年成立以来，他从未在联合国会场上以这样的傲慢口吻谈论联合国。凭借美国相当强大的经济和军事战略实力，世界大多数国家都怀着震惊与敬畏旁观这座巍峨的民主奥林匹斯山摇摇欲坠；它以难看的外表和不得体的语言凌驾于一切之上。如果唐纳德·特朗普破坏性独裁的影响仅限于美国及其周边邻国，事情本来会简单得多。事实并非如此。在自认为强大、实际上却害怕自身软弱的幻觉驱使下，特朗普对伊朗发动了一场模糊不清的战争。在其内阁中一班幼稚的部长，尤其是某个婴儿气的Pete Hegseth怂恿下，特朗普在过去八个月里向伊朗发射了不计其数的导弹、炸弹和无人机，其实际效果可疑得很，无非是一些亲犹太主义的征服宣传。当然，伊朗远未在任何意义上受到羞辱或击败。相反，美国在中东的所有盟友都被拖入了一场它们既未准备、也未曾设想的战争。迪拜、阿布扎比、多哈、安曼、利雅得等原本和平的地方，以及其他一些不太可能发生战事的地方，都成了伊朗无人机和火箭报复袭击的目标。特朗普总统及其伙伴、以色列的本雅明·内塔尼亚胡，应一己之欲将整个地区拖入战争；内塔尼亚胡因众多侵犯人权罪行在国际刑事法院受到通缉，在国内则面临多项贪腐指控。即使是欧洲等遥远地区，也承受了特朗普不得体的外交冒险带来的冲击。据称，特朗普在国内利用总统职权谋取腐败利益。众所周知，他的家族在世界各地经营着多项商业利益，而美国在这些地方也有利益。总统本人还参与内幕交易，交易对象是与美国政府有业务往来的公司。更不用说他在加密货币领域的多种骗局，以及委内瑞拉石油交易中的灰色勾当。如果唐纳德·特朗普执政期间的美国国内经济能让普通美国人过上价格合理、正常的生活，那么他的独裁倾向和惯常腐败就会相形见绌。恰恰相反，与伊朗无休止的战争已经使霍尔木兹海峡这一战略要道成为各国船只的死亡陷阱，并令石油货运对强国和弱国 alike 来说都成了噩梦。全球石油价格从此突破天花板。美国加油站油价从战前略高于$2的水平，飙至中期选举周超过$4的水平。杂货店价格也出现了类似涨幅。总体而言，所有两年前投票支持唐纳德·特朗普的人如今都在经济困境的痛苦中挣扎。因此，中期选举的结果非常可预测。这就是我们亲眼展开的现实。剩下的唯一任务，是通过中期选举检验美国的民主核心，从而把世界从“特朗普式终极噩梦”中拯救出来。这是对民主国家的一次历史性检验。美国选民再次被要求运用选票的力量，重新确认国会议员作为人民代表的授权，从而约束总统的独裁倾向。中期选举的意义正在于此：它是重新确认美国民主中民意的工具。在个人领导人与民主国家制度之间微妙的平衡中，作为民选领导人的特朗普占据了过重的分量。他实际上压倒了国家，并使其陷入失序。国会、司法部门、执法机构和联邦官僚体系，全都被迫扭曲，以迎合专横“国王”特朗普的意愿。在中期选举后的重建时期，总统与他已经破坏的制度之间将出现压力和紧张。首要问题将是获救的国家制度与专横总统顽固而特立独行的倾向之间的冲突。特朗普仍会顽固不化、好斗、辱骂他人、抗拒规则并倾向于违法。他会以“商业交易规则”为掩护，试图规避外交谈判和结构化接触的规则，为自己以及家人、朋友、同伙和走狗谋取利益。特朗普剩余的任期仍将由这个世界的Elon Musks主导。总体而言，刚刚结束的中期选举对特朗普政府的重创，是特朗普政治冒险及其历史性错位所产生的更广泛影响。两百多年来，美国一直是一个吸引世界各个角落人们的梦想。美国的吸引力在于其多样性、社会的自由，以及强大的创业精神；这种精神使每一个生活在美国的人都成为自由社会繁荣遗产的参与者。美国梦逐渐成为所有出生在美国或移居美国的人的共同梦想。简言之，美国梦的核心，是美国每个人都有权通过勤奋工作、专注抱负以及享有诚实劳动成果的权利，加入追求幸福的竞赛。然而就在我们眼前、就在我们有生之年，美国梦已经变成一场噩梦。这个曾被所有人视为自由与安全最后避难所的国家，变成了不受欢迎的炼狱。所谓非法移民正受到追猎，在美国各大城市四处逃窜，并在光天化日之下被未经训练且充满偏见的移民猎犬像疯狗一样射杀。以反移民为名，无辜的定居者——其中一些人在美国已经生活了三四十年——遭到追捕，被塞进军用飞机，遭驱逐返回他们多年前离开、早已没有记忆的国家。唐纳德·特朗普作为第二任期总统的统治，见证了美国区别于其他文明的各项特征遭到系统性侵蚀。如今它是一股黑暗力量，在国内外都意味着祸害。特朗普治下的美国成了一股反伊斯兰力量，却又是犹太主义的拥护者，一个偏见的白人至上主义堡垒。其社会沿着种族和认知界线分裂。美国中期选举或许成为制衡制度滑向独裁的必要措施。总统如今必须获得一个更多元化的国会的授权，才能继续勾连下去。然而，特朗普的独裁勾连给世界和美国制度造成的损害相当严重。他未经国会批准便发动战争。他在公海上杀人，却不願意证明这些人犯下了任何罪行。他仅凭自己的直觉便对主权国家发动残酷战争。他把航空母舰部署到世界各地海域，下令实施精确轰炸，只消给他那位幼稚的战争部长打一通电话，便允许部署先进导弹系统和战机。如今萦绕不去的问题是：在民主无人守护、遭受一个由民主选举产生却拒不悔改的暴君横冲直撞式进攻的疯狂年代里，世界如何从美国和世界遭受的巨大破坏中恢复？一项繁复的修复工程正以令人警惕的紧迫性摆在美国面前。民主礼仪的护栏需要重建。华盛顿需要重新培养得体的政治礼仪和言辞。最重要的是，美国必须摒弃总统职位中的那种粗俗作风，以至于把Mickey Minaj的臀部当作总统公开言论的话题。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary: A faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), led by former Minister of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, Kabiru Turaki, has said its legal team is reviewing the Court of Appeal judgement affirming the Wike-backed faction as the party’s authentic leadership. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary_zh: 人民民主党（PDP）的一个派别表示，其法律团队正在研究上诉法院维持由 Wike 支持的派别为该党合法领导机构的判决。前特别事务与政府间事务部长 Kabiru Turaki 领导该派别。上诉法院上周三作出的一致判决维持了联邦高等法院此前的裁决，即驳回针对人民民主党（PDP）由 Abdulrahman Mohammed 担任主席的 Wike 支持派别领导权提出的诉讼。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: A faction of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), led by former Minister of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, Kabiru Turaki, has said its legal team is reviewing the Court of Appeal judgement affirming the Wike-backed faction as the party’s authentic leadership. The faction said its lawyers would advise on whether to challenge the judgement at the Supreme Court after reviewing its legal implications. It, however, expressed optimism that it would eventually be recognised as the PDP’s authentic national leadership. Mr Turaki disclosed this on Saturday when a delegation of governorship candidates who had obtained nomination and expression of interest forms from his faction paid a solidarity visit to its leaders in Abuja. The candidates said the visit was aimed at encouraging the faction’s leadership to develop a strategic plan to sensitise and unite party members, particularly at the grassroots level. The candidates were Sunday Biggs (Plateau), Ladi Hassan (Kwara), Joel Danlami (Taraba), Caleb Myebangara (Adamawa), Isah Muqaddam (Gombe), Lawal Umar (Kaduna), Ibrahim Abdullahi (Kebbi), Yakubu Mu’azu (Jigawa) and Zanna Gaddama (Borno). Mr Turaki told the delegation that the faction would meet with its legal team to consider its assessment of the judgement before deciding on the next course of action. “I have listened to you carefully, and I want to inform you, and through you to inform Nigerians, that since our judgement last Wednesday, we’ve instructed our team of lawyers to study, say and advise us accordingly. “And I can confirm to you that immediately after this meeting, we’re going to have a meeting with our legal team and they’re going to tell us the result of their assessment of the judgement of the Court of Appeal,” he said. The Court of Appeal, in a unanimous judgement delivered last Wednesday, upheld the earlier decision of the Federal High Court dismissing a suit challenging the leadership of the Wike-backed faction of the PDP, chaired by Abdulrahman Mohammed. The three-member panel was presided over by Ugochukwu Ogakwu, with Laja Balogun and Ruqayyat—Ayoola, who read the judgment. The suit was instituted by the Board of Trustees (BoT) aligned with the Turaki faction. The board is chaired by Adolphus Wabara, a former Senate president. The appeal, marked CA/ABJ/CV/1221/2026, was filed by Mr Wabara and seven others against the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and six other respondents. The appellants had asked the court to set aside the Federal High Court judgment and compel INEC to recognise the Interim National Working Committee (NWC) led by Mr Turaki. They argued that the committee emerged from a National Executive Committee meeting convened after the Supreme Court judgment in April. However, the Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal, affirming the position of the lower court in favour of the Wike-backed faction. Mr Turaki told the governorship candidates that the faction would continue its efforts to take control of the party through constitutional and legal means. He expressed optimism that the Supreme Court would rule in its favour, paving the way for its candidates to participate in the 2027 general elections. He also predicted that the PDP would win the elections if the faction eventually secured recognition as the party’s authentic leadership. “I want to assure your excellencies and indeed your other colleagues who are not here, and through you also, to assure other candidates, our other respective candidates, that there is indeed going to be a bright sunny day at the end of the tournament. This struggle will continue. We are hopeful that we will win, and that after winning, PDP candidates shall be on the ballot. “And as soon as we are on the ballot, I want to assure you that Nigerians are waiting for us. We shall be winning the 2027 elections by the special grace of God. So on behalf of PDP, I want to thank you so very much for the continuous support, the solidarity that you’ve been giving to us,” he added. Mr Turaki thanked the candidates for their support and advice, assuring them that the faction would continue to work with them and other party organs in accordance with the party’s constitution. He accused unnamed forces of attempting to undermine the party, insisting that the faction would continue to resist efforts to place the PDP in bondage. “Now, PDP has come to stay, and PDP will continue to fight to free itself from the shackles of bondage that some undemocratic forces and elements are trying to put us in,” he said. He also urged the candidates to encourage their supporters to remain calm and hopeful despite the court’s decision. “I pray that God will grant you a journey back home with mercy, and then try to talk to your people to remain calm. Let them remain calm. Fighting is not for those who are seeing victory in sight. So we should not fight. “We should remain resolute. We should remain prepared, because even if it is a few days to the date of the election, and the shackles, the bondage of our party are freed, we will get to the polls. And by the special grace of God, we will emerge victorious,” he said. Speaking earlier on behalf of the delegation, Mr Biggs, the PDP governorship candidate in Plateau State, said the visit was intended to demonstrate solidarity with the faction’s leadership and encourage it to pursue all available legal options. “The visit was to interact with the INWC to show solidarity with them and to encourage them to undertake a strategic plan aimed at sensitising and unifying the party, especially at the grassroots level. “Furthermore, to ensure that the appeal to the Supreme Court is pursued with urgency, competence and every necessary legal preparation,” he said. Mr Biggs also urged the faction to explore reconciliation and constructive engagement with aggrieved members to resolve the party’s leadership crisis. “We also want them to establish a broader platform for reconciliation and constructive engagement among aggrieved members. The national publicity secretary should ensure that effective communication with party members is regularly held to prevent misinformation, speculation and unnecessary anxiety. “The party should develop a comprehensive political and organisational strategy to strengthen the party ahead of the 2027 general elections,” he said
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 人民民主党派系可能就承认Wike支持的领导层的上诉法院判决提出异议
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh:
人民民主党（PDP）的一个派系表示，其法律团队正在审议上诉法院维持由Wike支持的派系为该党合法领导层的判决。该派系称，在评估判决的法律影响后，其律师将就是否向最高法院提出挑战提供建议。不过，该派系乐观地认为，最终将获承认是该党合法的全国领导机构。图拉基周六透露了上述情况。当时，一批已从其派系取得州长候选人提名和意向书表格的州长候选人代表团前往阿布贾，对该派系领导人进行声援访问。候选人包括Sunday Biggs（普拉州）、Ladi Hassan（夸拉州）、Joel Danlami（塔拉巴州）、Caleb Myebangara（阿达瓦州）、Isah Muqaddam（贡贝州）、Lawal Umar（卡杜纳州）、Ibrahim Abdullahi（凯比州）、Yakubu Mu’azu（吉加瓦州）和Zanna Gaddama（博尔诺州）。图拉基告诉代表团，该派系将与法律团队会面，考虑其对判决的评估结果，再决定下一步行动。

“我已经认真听取了你们的意见。我想告诉你们，并通过你们告知尼日利亚人民，自上周三作出判决以来，我们已指示律师团队进行研究、提出意见并据此向我们提供建议。

“我可以向你们确认，这次会面结束后，我们将立即与法律团队开会，他们将告诉我们对上诉法院判决进行评估的结果。”他说。

上诉法院上周三以一致通过的判决维持了联邦高等法院此前的裁定，即驳回针对PDP由Wike支持的派系领导权提出的诉讼。该派系由Abdulrahman Mohammed担任主席。审判由三人小组进行，Ugochukwu Ogakwu主持，Laja Balogun和Ruqayyat—Ayoola参加，后者宣读了判决。该诉讼由与图拉基派系立场一致的受托人董事会提起。董事会由前参议院议长Adolphus Wabara主持。编号为CA/ABJ/CV/1221/2026的上诉由Wabara先生等8人针对独立国家选举委员会（INEC）及其他6名被上诉人提出。上诉人请求法院撤销联邦高等法院的判决，并强制INEC承认由图拉基先生领导的临时全国工作委员会（NWC）。他们主张，该委员会是在最高法院于4月作出判决后召开的全国执行委员会会议上产生的。然而，上诉法院驳回了上诉，维持了下级法院支持Wike支持派系的立场。

图拉基告诉州长候选人，该派系将继续通过符合党章和法律的手段争取掌控该党。他乐观地认为，最高法院将作出有利于该派系的裁决，为其候选人参加2027年大选铺平道路。他还预言，如果该派系最终获承认是该党的合法领导机构，PDP将赢得此次选举。

“我想向各位阁下，以及确实向今天不在场的其他同事，并通过你们向其他候选人和我们各自的其他候选人保证，赛事终将有阳光灿烂的一天。这场斗争还将继续。我们希望能够获胜，获胜后，PDP候选人将出现在选票上。

“而且，一旦我们出现在选票上，我要向你们保证，尼日利亚人民正在等待我们。凭借上帝的特别恩典，我们将赢得2027年选举。因此，我谨代表PDP向你们致以最诚挚的感谢，感谢你们一直以来的支持和声援。”他补充说。

图拉基感谢候选人的支持和建议，并保证该派系将继续依照党章与他们及该党其他机构合作。他指责一些未具名势力企图破坏该党，并坚持称该派系将继续抵抗使PDP陷入束缚的企图。

“现在，PDP已经站稳脚跟，PDP将继续抗争，摆脱一些不民主势力和因素企图加诸我们身上的奴役枷锁。”他说。

他还敦促候选人鼓励支持者，尽管法院作出了判决，仍应保持冷静和希望。

“我祈祷上帝以恩典护送你们平安回家，然后设法告诉你们的人民保持平静。让他们保持平静。胜利已在望的人不需要战斗。因此，我们不应争斗。

“我们应保持坚定，应做好准备，因为即使距离选举日只有几天，即使我们党所受的枷锁和束缚得以解除，我们仍会走进投票站。凭借上帝的特别恩典，我们将取得胜利。”他说。

此前，代表团发言人、PDP普拉州州长候选人Biggs先生表示，此次访问旨在向该派系领导人表达声援，并鼓励其采取一切可用的法律行动。

“此次访问是为了与NWC交流，向他们表达声援，并鼓励他们制定战略计划，推动全党上下开展宣传和团结工作，尤其是在基层层面。

“此外，还要确保及时、熟练且做好一切必要法律准备地向最高法院提出上诉。”他说。

Biggs先生还敦促该派系探索和解及与心怀不满的成员开展建设性接触，以解决该党的领导层危机。

He explained that the next phase of his government's development agenda would prioritise ensuring that citizens could secure decent and dignified means of livelihood. “In this presentation, we will outline our plan for what we call the New Economy. This is a bold initiative that will seek to invest over $9 billion in job-rich sectors of the economy between 2027 and 2030. “The Volta Region is expected to benefit greatly under the New Economy policy, particularly in the areas of textiles, garments, commercial agriculture, hospitality and tourism,” he said. President Mahama noted that these sectors had been selected because of their capacity to boost economic activity and generate employment, particularly in the Volta Region. The President also acknowledged ongoing development projects in various districts, including the construction of health facilities, classroom blocks and feeder roads, financed through the District Assemblies Common Fund. He attributed the increased financial resources available to district assemblies to a directive issued shortly after he assumed office, which requires that at least 80 per cent of the District Assemblies Common Fund be transferred directly to district administrations to facilitate development at the local level

https://www.myjoyonline.com/seven-compan.body: President John Mahama has announced that seven companies have been shortlisted for the development of the Keta Port in the Volta Region. The companies were selected from 47 that submitted expressions of interest to partner with the Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) as strategic partners for the project. Addressing the 2026 Hogbetsotso Festival, President Mahama said the shortlisted companies have successfully completed the due diligence stage and will now proceed to the next phase of the process. He explained that the next stage would involve completing the designs and securing financing to pave the way for construction to begin. “Due diligence has been conducted, and the list has been shortlisted to seven companies. These seven companies are proceeding to the next stage, which involves completing the designs and arranging the financing for the project to commence,” he said. The President also disclosed that the administration block for the port, which was started under the previous administration, is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 2027. “Government remains committed to advancing the project on a credible foundation,” he assured. On other development projects in the Volta Region, President Mahama announced that the Sogakope-Agodome-Keta Water Project, which stalled following Ghana's debt restructuring, is expected to resume. He said the government signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the contractors in October to facilitate their return to site and the completion of the first phase. On road infrastructure, President Mahama said the Ho-Denu Road is progressing steadily and is expected to be completed in 2027. He added that procurement processes are underway for the reconstruction of the road from Central University at Miotso, near Dawhenya, to Aflao. The government is also working to secure a contractor for the Dabala-Savietula-Keta-Denu Highway. President Mahama further disclosed that several roads in the Anlo area, including the Abor-Atiavi road, has been captured under the World Bank Feeder Roads Project, with procurement expected to begin soon. On healthcare, he said discussions have been initiated during his recent visit to Korea for the resumption of financing for the upgrade of the Volta Regional Hospital in Ho. He said the upgrade would ensure that the facility is befitting of a teaching hospital. The President also announced progress towards establishing a School of Pharmacy under the University of Health and Allied Sciences (UHAS), saying land had been secured and inspected by the committee overseeing its establishment. He said the next steps would involve designing the campus and proceeding to procurement. President Mahama also pledged to support other educational infrastructure requests in the region, including a new dormitory block for Anlo-Afiadenyigba Senior High School, proposed E-Blocks for Shime and Anlo Senior High Schools, and infrastructure improvements at Atiavi Senior High School and Technical School. He further acknowledged calls for the upgrading of Ohawu Agricultural College into a university. On housing, the President said an additional GH¢500 million has been allocated for district housing projects and assured the people of Anlo that the area would benefit. He also said the Anloga 24-hour market project is on track, while preparations for the proposed Aflao Ashigame market have advanced, with land secured and designs completed. According to him, a technical team from China, financed through a grant from the Chinese Government, is expected to visit the project sites to confirm the designs before the release of a US$30 million grant to commence the project. President Mahama urged the Volta Regional Coordinating Council to closely monitor the implementation of the various projects to ensure their timely delivery

Unlock these with Subscription An ancient mound in Bihar's East Champaran district has been declared an archaeological site of national importance through a central government notification. The site – Ranivas Mound, at Kesariya – is spread over 1.63 acres and is under the ownership of the Bihar government, reads the gazette notification dated November 4 that was issued by the Ministry of Culture. Copies of the said notification were made available to the public on June 8, 2026 and "no objection has been received" from any person with regard to the declaration by the central government, said the notification signed by Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Director General Yadubir Singh Rawat. A copy of the notification was affixed at a conspicuous place as required under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains (AMASR) Act, 1958. A total of 3,686 sites around the country are under the care of the ASI, the Centre had informed Parliament in February 2026. A recommendation for listing the ancient Ranivas mound in Bihar as a centrally protected monument was sent to ASI headquarters in Delhi in 2021, a senior official told PTI in September 2022. According to the existing procedure, proposals or recommendations sent by regional ASI circles are examined by a team at the organisation’s headquarters before a final decision is taken on naming them monuments or sites of national importance. In case of meritorious proposals and recommendations, a provisional notification is first made, followed by the issuance of a final gazetted notification. A senior official said the inclusion of new sites under the ambit of the ASI is an ongoing process, based on recommendations received from various ASI “circles”, or regions, across the country from time to time. Centrally protected sites in Bihar fall under the jurisdiction of the ASI’s Patna Circle. Currently, 70 sites in Bihar are under the ambit of the ASI and governed by the Patna Circle, which is one of the oldest regional circles in India. The Patna Circle was earlier known as the Mid-Eastern Circle, and still earlier as the Buddhist Circle, ostensibly because of the important Buddhist monuments lying in the area, according to the Circle’s website. The ruins of the ancient Nalanda University in Bihar, also under the ASI, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The ancestral house of India’s first president Rajendra Prasad in Ziradei, Siwan, north Bihar, was officially declared a protected monument on May 27, 1991. Its provisional notification was done on October 30, 1990. The Shiva Temple in Gaya was notified by the ASI in 1996. Since then, no fresh site in Bihar had been brought under the ambit of the ASI, the senior official had said in September 2022. The Patna Circle earlier covered Jharkhand and a large number of sites in eastern Uttar Pradesh. While the Ranchi Circle was created in 2003 after Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar in 2000, a separate Sarnath Circle was created in 2013 for sites falling in eastern Uttar Pradesh. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/b.body_zh: 订阅账户还可享受 Premium Stories、Editorials、Opinions 等内容。订阅即可解锁这些内容。印度比哈尔邦东昌帕兰县的一座古土丘，经中央政府发布通知，已被宣布为国家重要考古遗址。文化和旅游部于11月4日发布的官方公报通知称，该遗址位于克萨里亚的拉尼瓦斯土丘，占地1.63英亩，归比哈尔邦政府所有。通知副本于2026年6月8日向社会公开，并由印度考古局（ASI）总监察长亚杜比尔·辛格·拉瓦特签署。通知称，中央政府作出这一宣布后，“未收到任何人的异议”。根据《1958年古迹与考古遗址及遗迹法》（AMASR Act, 1958）第4条第（1）款的规定，通知副本已张贴在显著位置。2026年2月，中央政府告知议会，全国共有3,686处遗址由印度考古局负责管理。2022年9月，一名高级官员告诉印度报业托拉斯（PTI），将比哈尔邦古老的拉尼瓦斯土丘列为中央保护古迹的建议，于2021年送交位于德里的印度考古局总部。按照现行程序，各地区印度考古局分局提交的提案或建议，均由该机构总部的团队审查，之后再就是否将其命名为国家重要古迹或遗址作出最终决定。对于有价值的提案和建议，首先会发布临时通知，随后发布正式的官方公报通知。一名高级官员称，将新遗址纳入印度考古局管理范围是一项持续进行的工作，依据的是该局各分局或地区不时提交的建议。印度考古局在比哈尔邦管理的中央保护遗址，隶属该局巴特那分局管辖。目前，比哈尔邦有70处遗址纳入印度考古局的管理范围，由巴特那分局负责监管；该分局是印度历史最悠久的地区分局之一。据该分局网站称，巴特那分局此前称为中东部分局，更早时称为佛教分局，表面上是因为该地区分布着重要的佛教古迹。同样由印度考古局管理的比哈尔邦古老那烂陀大学遗址，是联合国教科文组织世界遗产。印度首任总统拉金德拉·普拉萨德位于比哈尔邦北部锡万县齐拉代伊的祖居，于1991年5月27日正式宣布为受保护古迹，其临时通知于1990年10月30日发布。加亚的湿婆神庙于1996年被印度考古局列入通知名录。这名高级官员曾在2022年9月表示，自那以后，比哈尔邦没有新增遗址纳入印度考古局的管理范围。巴特那分局此前还负责贾坎德邦以及北方邦东部的大量遗址。2000年贾坎德邦从比哈尔邦分出后，兰契分局于2003年成立；2013年，又为北方邦东部境内的遗址成立了萨纳特分局。印度考古局成立于1861年，亚历山大·坎宁安担任该机构首任负责人。评论必须使用英文，并以完整句子表述。评论不得含有辱骂性内容或针对个人的攻击。请遵守我们的社区评论指南。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已是《The Hindu》的注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与我们的文章互动。如果你还没有账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录自己的账户后，可以查看此前在 Vuukle 上发表的旧评论。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/npp-usa-elec.body: A member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP)’s United States branch, Opoku Boateng, has called for in-person voting and an immediate election timetable as the November 30 deadline for outstanding party polls approaches. In a statement, he raised concerns about what he described as inadequate communication from the committee overseeing the NPP-USA elections. According to Mr Boateng, members have yet to receive an election date, a published timetable or information on the register of eligible voters. “Members are not asking for miracles. They are asking for a timetable,” he said. He cited an October 29, 2026, directive by NPP General Secretary Justin Kodua requiring all outstanding elections to be completed by November 30. Mr Boateng argued that the lack of a clear roadmap was making it difficult for members to prepare and for candidates to organise their campaigns. The statement said the NPP-USA election was initially expected in July 2026 but was postponed after disagreements over an electronic voting system developed by NPP Ghana. According to Mr Boateng, members questioned the platform’s independence and raised concerns that it had not been tested in Ghana's elections. “It is important to understand that rejecting a particular voting platform does not mean rejecting democracy, technology, or the desire to elect leaders,” he said. As an alternative, he proposed voting at the various chapters, with results subsequently collated at the NPP-USA branch level. He also called for consideration of a regulated proxy voting arrangement for members unable to attend physically. He said this should include verification and accountability measures to prevent duplication, impersonation, and abuse. “The proposal is not intended to complicate the election. It is intended to build confidence,” he said. Mr Boateng also questioned how the electoral committee had been constituted. He alleged that the General Secretary established it directly, without the expected consultation with NPP-USA executives. He urged the committee to engage chapter leaders, executives, candidates and members to address concerns and build confidence in the process. His demands include publishing the voter register, allowing members to verify their eligibility and clarifying voting and results-collation procedures. He cautioned against waiting until the final days before the deadline to announce arrangements. “A credible election cannot be organised through last-minute announcements, hurried arrangements, and inadequate communication,” he said. While acknowledging the importance of meeting the deadline, Mr Boateng said speed should not come at the expense of fairness. He appealed to members to remain united despite differences over candidates and voting methods, saying the priority should be an election that strengthens the branch

Unlock these with Subscription Hundreds of students under the aegis of All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) staged a protest at Vivekananda Circle in Dharwad on Friday, condemning the State government’s move to allow adoption of government schools by private institutions and corporate companies. Addressing the protesters, AIDSO district secretary Shashikala Meti alleged that the Congress government, which had promised to protect government schools, was pursuing policies such as the Karnataka Public Schools (KPS)-Magnet initiative and an agreement with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) that would undermine the public education system. She alleged that the government had held a meeting at Vidhana Soudha on November 4 to facilitate the handing over of government schools to private institutions and corporate companies, with 2,000 schools proposed to be taken up in the first phase. She termed the move a betrayal of the people. Ms. Meti also criticised Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and the government representatives for allegedly making derogatory remarks about government school teachers and blaming them for declining educational standards, while overlooking shortcomings in its own policies. She said the government was proposing that private institutions adopt three government schools each, with the provision to name the schools after the adopting institutions. Other proposals reportedly included deputing teachers from private schools and providing old buses, laboratory equipment and computers. The government should address deficiencies in public education and recruit adequate numbers of teachers instead of shifting its responsibility to private entities, she said. Ms. Meti alleged that 14 government schools had already been merged with the KPS at Hegganuru in Kanakapura, Bengaluru South district, contradicting the government’s assurance that no government school would be closed. She demanded the immediate withdrawal of the government’s education policies and called upon the public to join a movement against what she termed the “corporate takeover” of public education. AIDSO district president Sindhu Kou di, district organisers Shantesh Nandikollam, Siddalingappa Chippalakatti and Ravishankar Poladi, among others took part in the protest. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body: A senior North Korean ruling party official has met his counterpart in Beijing, the North's state media said Saturday, the latest in a series of high-level meetings during his visit this week. Kim Song-nam, a Political Bureau member and Central Committee secretary of North Korea's Workers' Party of Korea (WPA), met Liu Haixing, head of the Communist Party of China's (CPC) Central Committee's International Liaison Department, at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse on Friday, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said. It was Kim's third meeting with a senior Chinese official since he arrived Tuesday, as the two countries are seeking to deepen ties and expand cooperation after Chinese President Xi Jinping's June summit with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in Pyongyang. Kim briefed Liu on Pyongyang's "successes" in party-building work and said the whole country has been striving to meet the targets of the five-year plan adopted at the party's ninth congress in February. For his part, Liu called the visit significant for strengthening relations, according to the report. The two sides reaffirmed support for each other's policies and pledged deeper cooperation. Following the meeting, China hosted a reception for the North Korean delegation. In a separate dispatch, the KCNA said Kim also met Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau and director of its General Office, on Friday. At the meeting, Kim reaffirmed Pyongyang's commitment to closer ties. Kim began his high-level meetings Thursday with Foreign Minister Wang Yi. His delegation arrived in Beijing as the two countries seek to shore up cooperation after relations appeared to cool amid North Korea's deepening alignment with Russia over the war in Ukraine

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffa.body_zh: 据朝鲜官方媒体周六报道，朝鲜执政党一名高级官员在北京会见了中方对口官员，这是他本周访问期间一系列高层会晤中的最新一次。朝鲜劳动党中央政治局委员兼中央委员会书记金松南周五在钓鱼台国宾馆会见了中共中央对外联络部部长刘海星，朝鲜中央通讯社报道称。这是金松南自周二抵达以来第三次会见中国高级官员，当时两国正寻求在今年6月中国国家主席习近平与朝鲜领导人金正恩在平壤举行峰会后深化关系并扩大合作。金松南向刘海星介绍了平壤在党建工作方面取得的“成就”，并表示全国上下都在努力实现党第九次代表大会2月通过的五年计划目标。刘海星则表示此次访问对加强两国关系具有重要意义，双方重申支持彼此的政策并承诺深化合作。会晤结束后，中方为朝鲜代表团举行了招待会。朝鲜中央通讯社在另一篇报道中称，金松南周五还与中共中央政治局常委、中央办公厅主任蔡奇举行了会晤。会晤中，金松南重申了平壤致力于加强两国关系的承诺。金松南于周四开始高层会晤，首先会见了外交部长王毅。他的代表团抵达北京之际，两国正寻求加强合作，此前因朝鲜在乌克兰战争中与俄罗斯加深结盟而使双边关系显得有所冷却。

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: NEW YORK — AI stocks are bouncing back Friday and recovering some of their sell-off from the last two days. The rest of the U.S. stock market is mixed following a whirlwind few days of Wall Street trying to sort out what this week’s sweeping victories by Democrats in the U.S. midterm elections will mean for the economy. The S&P 500 rose 0.9 percent and trimmed its loss for the week to 2.1 percent. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 3 points, or less than 0.1 percent, as of 11:45 a.m. Eastern time, and the Nasdaq composite was 1.6 percent higher. Even with this week's extreme swings, the S&P 500 remains only 5.1 percent below its all-time high, which was set last month. It and other companies tied to the build-out of AI data centers tumbled this week on worries that Democratic victories in statehouses across the country could mean a slowdown in further construction, particularly in Texas. Voters across political parties say they’re wary about AI and don’t like increases to power bills caused by data centers. That built on top of worries already rattling the industry that further construction of AI data centers may slow because of how expensive it’s become to borrow money. Before that, even, critics were saying AI stock prices had shot too high and were in a bubble. But political power in Washington will still be split between a Democratic Congress and a White House run by the Republican Trump, who retains the power to veto. That could limit federal efforts to rein in the AI industry. In the meantime, companies in the industry still see strong growth. IREN, a company that delivers data centers, compute and software for AI training, reported stronger results for the latest quarter than analysts expected. Its stock jumped 19.5 percent, and it also announced two new contracts signed since the end of the quarter. “We own the land, the power and the data centers under all of it, which gives us more ways to fund growth and lets us set its pace,” co-CEO Daniel Roberts said. Lam Research, a company whose equipment and services help make semiconductors, climbed 9.9 percent after announcing a program to send up to $25 billion to its investors by buying back shares of its own stock. That helped other stocks that have benefited from the build-out of AI data centers recover some of their own sharp losses. CoreWeave, which rents out access to AI chips to customers over the cloud, rose 4.5 percent. Micron Technology, which sells memory for computers, climbed 5.9 percent. Outside of AI, the U.S. stock market was mixed, and slightly more stocks fell within the S&P 500 than rose. Axon Enterprise tumbled 17.6 percent after the seller of Tasers reported weaker results for the latest quarter than analysts expected. It also announced a $1.2 billion investment in Skydio, a drone technology company. Charter Communications sank 5 percent after the internet and video provider reported a loss for the latest quarter, when analysts were expecting a profit. In the bond market, Treasury yields recovered some of their sharp drops from earlier in the week, triggered by tumbling stock prices and hopes that split control of Washington could limit how much more the U.S. government adds to its debt. The yield on the 10-year Treasury edged up to 4.85 percent from 4.84 percent late Thursday. It had topped 5.30 percent last month when worries about inflation, higher interest rates and rising government debt were spiking. Helping to support yields was a report showing U.S. employers hired many more workers last month than economists expected. It’s the latest signal that the U.S. economy continues to chug along despite high inflation. On one hand, the encouraging data could mean the U.S. economy may be able to absorb a slowdown in construction of AI data centers. But at the same time, the strong growth in jobs could push upward on inflation. Following the report, traders saw a greater probability of the Federal Reserve hiking its short-term interest rate at its next meeting in December, according to data from CME Group. Rate hikes by the Fed can rein in inflation, but they do so by making borrowing money more expensive for everyone and slowing the overall economy. A separate report, meanwhile, suggested that sentiment among U.S. consumers unexpectedly improved. The preliminary report from the University of Michigan said sentiment rose for lower- and middle-wealth Americans but fell for those with the largest stock portfolios. Perhaps more importantly for the bond market, the survey also suggested expectations for inflation in the coming year eased for Americans. That could prevent a vicious cycle where expectations for high inflation drive behavior that only worsens inflation
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 人工智能概念股遭全球抛售，华尔街本周跌幅收窄
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 纽约消息——人工智能股票周五反弹，收复了过去两天抛售的部分跌幅。在华尔街经历了一连串跌宕起伏、试图判断本周民主党在美国中期选举中取得广泛胜利将如何影响经济之后，美国股市其余板块涨跌互现。标普500指数上涨0.9%，全周跌幅收窄至2.1%。截至东部时间上午11时45分，道琼斯工业平均指数下跌3点，跌幅不足0.1%；纳斯达克综合指数上涨1.6%。尽管本周行情剧烈波动，标普500指数仍仅比上月创下的历史高点低5.1%。该指数成分股及其他与人工智能数据中心建设相关的公司本周重挫，原因包括担心民主党在全国各州议会获胜可能意味着进一步建设放缓，尤其是在得克萨斯州。各政治派别的选民表示，他们对人工智能持谨慎态度，也不喜欢数据中心推高电费。这一因素又叠加了已经令该行业不安的担忧：由于借贷成本大幅上升，人工智能数据中心的进一步建设可能放缓。此前，甚至已有批评者称人工智能股票价格涨得过高，存在泡沫。不过，华盛顿的政治权力仍将由民主党控制的国会和共和党人特朗普掌控的白宫分享，特朗普仍保留否决权。这可能限制联邦政府监管人工智能行业的努力。与此同时，该行业公司仍预计将实现强劲增长。IREN是一家提供人工智能训练所需数据中心、算力和软件的公司，其最新季度业绩好于分析师预期。该公司股价上涨19.5%，并宣布在季度结束后又签署了两份新合同。联席首席执行官丹尼尔·罗伯茨说：“我们拥有土地、电力以及贯穿其中的数据中心，这使我们有更多方式为增长提供资金，也能自行掌控增长速度。”半导体制造设备和服务企业Lam Research宣布一项计划，通过回购自身股票向投资者返还最多250亿美元后，股价上涨9.9%。这也帮助其他受益于人工智能数据中心建设的股票收复了部分大幅跌幅。CoreWeave通过云端向客户提供人工智能芯片使用服务，股价上涨4.5%。销售计算机存储芯片的美光科技上涨5.9%。人工智能板块之外，美国股市涨跌互现，标普500指数成分股中下跌股票略多于上涨股票。Taser制造商Axon Enterprise最新季度业绩不及分析师预期，股价暴跌17.6%。该公司还宣布向无人机技术企业Skydio投资12亿美元。互联网和视频服务提供商Charter Communications最新季度出现亏损，而分析师原本预计其将实现盈利，股价下跌5%。债券市场上，美国国债收益率从本周早些时候的急跌中有所回升；此前股市暴跌，加之市场希望华盛顿的分裂格局能够限制美国政府进一步增加债务，均对收益率走势产生影响。10年期美国国债收益率从周四晚间的4.84%小幅升至4.85%。上月，在通胀、利率上升和政府债务攀升的担忧推动下，该收益率一度突破5.30%。一份报告显示，美国雇主上月招聘的 workers数量远多于经济学家预期，为收益率提供支撑。这是尽管通胀高企，美国经济仍在缓慢运行的最新迹象。一方面，这一令人鼓舞的数据可能意味着美国经济能够承受人工智能数据中心建设放缓；但另一方面，就业的强劲增长可能推高通胀。报告发布后，根据CME Group的数据，交易员认为美联储在12月下一次会议上上调短期利率的可能性更大。美联储加息能够抑制通胀，但方式是提高所有人的借贷成本，并拖累整体经济。与此同时，另一份报告显示，美国消费者信心意外改善。密歇根大学的初步报告称，中低收入和中等财富美国人的信心上升，但股票投资组合规模最大的群体信心下降Perhaps对债券市场而言更重要的是，调查还显示，美国人对未来一年通胀的预期有所缓和。这可能避免形成恶性循环：高通胀预期驱动相关行为，而这些行为只会进一步加剧通胀

Unlock these with Subscription Mysuru has figured in the list of cities adjudged for the Swachh Survekshan-2025-26 awards, with the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) receiving a formal invitation from the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to attend the award presentation ceremony scheduled to be held in New Delhi on November 11. The invitation marks Mysuru’s inclusion in the national-level recognition for urban cleanliness and sanitation. The prestigious Swachh Survekshan-2026 awards would be presented by President Droupadi Murmu at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi. However, there is no official information yet on the category in which Mysuru has been selected for an award or the rank it has secured. The details will be known only after the rankings and award categories are officially announced. In 2024-25, Mysuru was ranked 3rd cleanest city in India in the 3 to 10 lakh population category under Super Swachh League (SSL), which was a newly introduced category. Mysuru was ranked the cleanest city in India for two consecutive years – 2015 and 2016. MCC Commissioner M.K. Savita and a team of officers are visiting New Delhi for the award function. Minister in-charge of Mysuru district and Urban Development Minister Yathindra Siddaramaiah and senior officials were also expected to attend the function, sources in MCC said. Expressing happiness over the invitation, Ms. Savitha credited Mysuru’s cleanliness initiatives over the years to the collective efforts of former commissioners, health officials, pourakarmikas, and engineers, who, had worked together as a team to address the shortcomings identified in earlier surveys to bring recognition to the city. The MCC Commissioner said that the 11th edition of Swachh Survekshan had commenced and expressed hope that Mysuru would secure a good position in the 2026-27 survey as well. The 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan-2025-26 was conducted under the theme ‘Swachhata Ki Nayi Pehel – Badhayein Haath, Karein Safai Saath’. Mysuru MP Yaduveer Krishnadatta Chamaraja Wadiyar expressed happiness over the MCC being invited to the Swachh Survekshan award function and congratulated pourakarmikas and citizens for their efforts. “Let us all work together to further enhance Mysuru’s reputation on the cleanliness front,” he added. “This is a proud moment for the State. Official announcement of the ranking is awaited. I congratulate the pourakarmikas, MCC officials, staff and citizens of Mysuru ahead of the award presentation,” said the Urban Development Minister, in a statement. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body: Nigeria has recorded about 160 operational Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) refuelling stations across the country, with another 170 facilities at various stages of development and licensing, as the federal government intensifies efforts to expand access to cheaper alternative fuel. The Executive Chairman of the Presidential Compressed Natural Gas Initiative (PCNGI), Ismaeel Ahmed, disclosed this on Friday during the commissioning of a CNG Integrated Refuelling Unit (IRU) station along New Karu Road, Saint George Akume Way, Karu, Abuja. Mr Ahmed said the initiative had attracted approximately $2.6 billion in private-sector investments in less than two years, describing the growing investor interest as evidence that the market had moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage. “This is almost our 106th station across the country in less than two years. This is not beginning any longer. The market has been proven, and investors are trooping in,” he said. He said the additional stations were undergoing development or awaiting various approvals and licences from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority ( NMDPRA ). According to him, President Bola Tinubu has also directed another round of infrastructure deployment, including 1,500 units in February and an additional 500 in August, which are expected to come on stream between this year and early next year. Mr Ahmed said the expansion was necessary to accelerate the adoption of CNG in a country with more than 220 million people and approximately 12 million vehicles. He argued that Nigeria needed to move faster in developing alternative fuel infrastructure to meet the country’s transportation and energy demands. “It took Nigeria about 60 years to build approximately 24,000 conventional petrol stations, most of which are privately owned. We are seeing a much faster adoption of CNG and electric vehicles, and the scale of interest is encouraging,” he said. The PCNGI chairman argued that the adoption of CNG-powered vehicles had reduced transportation fares by between 30 and 40 per cent on some routes where the buses were already operating. He cited Abuja, Lagos and Kano, as well as inter-state routes between Kano and Katsina, as locations where passengers were benefiting from lower transportation costs. According to him, passengers who previously paid between N3,000 and N4,000 on some routes now pay about N1,500 when travelling in CNG-powered buses. He said the initiative was designed to extend the benefits to all local government areas, particularly those with high concentrations of commercial vehicles and passenger traffic. However, acknowledging that the existing fleet remained insufficient to meet demand, Mr Ahmed said the government was working to deploy more buses and expand access to the alternative fuel. Asked how the government arrived at the reported 30–40 per cent reduction in transportation fares, he said the figures were based on comparisons between fares charged by operators before and after the introduction of CNG-powered buses on selected routes. He explained that the initiative obtained information from transport operators about previous fares and compared them with the fares charged after the adoption of CNG. Also speaking at the commissioning ceremony , the Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Fashedemi, said the facility demonstrated the federal government’s commitment to promoting CNG as a cheaper alternative to petrol following the removal of the petrol subsidy. Mr Fashedemi said President Tinubu’s administration had introduced CNG as part of efforts to cushion the impact of subsidy removal on Nigerians, particularly in the transportation and energy sectors. He said Nigeria’s abundant natural gas resources, which had historically been underutilised and flared, presented an opportunity to provide cheaper energy alternatives for households and businesses. According to him, the State House decided to demonstrate the viability of the initiative by rehabilitating an abandoned fuel depot within its premises and converting it into a CNG refuelling facility. He explained that the government partnered with the PCNGI and selected Rolling Energy Limited as the private-sector operator to rehabilitate and upgrade the facility. Mr Fashedemi said the State House provided the existing infrastructure and location, while the private-sector partner financed the rehabilitation and upgrading of the facility. “The State House did not spend public funds on the facility. We provided the infrastructure and made the location available, while the private-sector partner invested in rehabilitating and upgrading it,” he said. He added that the facility also housed a vehicle conversion centre where motorists could convert eligible vehicles to run on CNG. The permanent secretary disclosed that the State House had acquired some hybrid vehicles, while some buses operating within the Villa premises also run on alternative energy. He said some State House employees would also bring their vehicles for conversion in the coming weeks, subject to technical assessments to determine their suitability. Mr Fashedemi said the initiative was intended to demonstrate that the government was willing to lead by example rather than merely advocate the adoption of alternative fuels. He urged private investors to take advantage of the opportunities in the CNG market, noting that government support through infrastructure partnerships could accelerate the expansion of refuelling facilities. Meanwhile, the Chief Executive Officer of Rolling Energy Limited, Mubarak Danbatta, described the project as an example of the benefits of collaboration between government and private investors. Mr Danbatta commended the State House for making the abandoned facility available for redevelopment, saying the partnership demonstrated how the government could facilitate private investment by providing access to existing infrastructure. “What you are seeing here is the power of partnership. When private entities and governments come together, this is the result,” he said. He explained that the facility, known as an Integrated Refuelling Unit, combined the dispenser and compressor in a single system, with double-nozzle dispensers that allow vehicles to refuel from both sides. According to him, the station has the capacity to serve approximately 150 vehicles daily, depending on cylinder size and pressure. Its vehicle conversion centre is also projected to convert about 12 vehicles daily. The growing investment in CNG infrastructure comes as Nigeria seeks to diversify its energy mix and reduce dependence on petrol, particularly following the removal of fuel subsidies in May 2023. The Tinubu-led administration has repeatedly argued that the adoption of the CNG technology is part of the broader effort to reduce high cost of living pressures on Nigerians due to some of the ongoing reforms initiated by the government
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.title_zh: 尼日利亚已有160座运营中的压缩天然气站，私人投资达到26亿美元
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/business/.body_zh: 尼日利亚全国目前约有160座投入运营的压缩天然气（CNG）加气站，另有170座设施处于开发或牌照审批的不同阶段。联邦政府正加大努力，扩大民众获得这种更廉价替代燃料的渠道。总统压缩天然气倡议（PCNGI）执行主席Ismaeel Ahmed于周五在阿布贾卡鲁区Saint George Akume Way新卡鲁路沿线一座压缩天然气综合加气单元（IRU）加气站投入使用时透露了上述数据。Ahmed先生表示，不到两年时间，该倡议便吸引了约26亿美元的私人部门投资，并将投资者兴趣日益增长形容为市场已超越概念验证阶段的证据。他说：“这几乎是我们不到两年在全国建成的第106座加气站。这已经不再只是开端。市场已经得到验证，投资者正在纷至沓来。”他说，其他加气站正在开发之中，或等待尼日利亚中游及下游石油监管局（NMDPRA）的各项审批和许可。据他介绍，总统Bola Tinubu还指示开展新一轮基础设施建设，包括2月部署1,500个加气单元，8月再增加500个，预计这些设施将在今年至明年初陆续投入运营。Ahmed先生表示，在一个拥有超过2.2亿人口和约1,200万辆汽车的国家，扩大压缩天然气基础设施对于加快其普及至关重要。他认为，尼日利亚需要加快发展替代燃料基础设施，以满足国内交通和能源需求。他说：“尼日利亚花了约60年才建成约24,000座传统加油站，其中大多数为私营。我们如今看到压缩天然气和电动汽车的普及速度要快得多，关注度之广令人鼓舞。”PCNGI主席表示，在已经运营压缩天然气公交车的部分线路上，使用压缩天然气为燃料的车辆使交通票价降低了30%至40%。他列举了阿布贾、拉各斯和卡诺，以及卡诺与卡茨纳之间的州际线路，称这些地方的乘客正受益于较低的出行成本。据他介绍，此前乘客在部分线路需支付3,000至4,000奈拉，如今乘坐压缩天然气公交车只需支付约1,500奈拉。他说，该倡议旨在将相关惠益拓展至所有地方政府辖区，尤其是商用车辆和客流量高度集中的地区。不过，Ahmed先生承认现有车队仍不足以满足需求，政府正着手部署更多公交车并扩大替代燃料的可及性。当被问及政府如何得出交通票价降低30%至40%的数据时，他表示，这些数字来自对运营商在部分线路引入压缩天然气公交车前后所收取票价的比较。他解释说，该倡议向运输运营商收集以往票价信息，并将其与采用压缩天然气后收取的票价进行比较。州府常务秘书Temitope Fashedemi也出席启用仪式并表示，在取消汽油补贴后，这座设施体现了联邦政府推动压缩天然气作为汽油廉价替代燃料的承诺。Fashedemi先生说，Tinubu总统政府将压缩天然气纳入相关措施，旨在缓冲取消补贴对尼日利亚民众造成的影响，尤其是在交通和能源领域。他说，尼日利亚丰富的天然气资源过去长期未得到充分利用，部分天然气还被火炬燃烧，这为家庭和企业提供更廉价的能源替代方案创造了机会。据他介绍，州府决定通过修复其院区内一座废弃油库并将其改造为压缩天然气加气设施来展示该倡议的可行性。他解释说，政府与PCNGI合作，并选择Rolling Energy Limited担任私营部门运营商，负责修复和升级该设施。Fashedemi先生说，州府提供现有基础设施和场地，而私营部门合作伙伴出资完成设施修复与升级。他说：“州府没有为这座设施动用公共资金。我们提供了基础设施并提供了场地，而私营部门合作伙伴投资修复和升级了它。”他还补充称，该设施内还设有一座车辆改装中心，驾车者可在那里将符合条件的车辆改装为使用压缩天然气。常务秘书透露，州府已购入一些混合动力汽车，府邸内运营的部分公交车也使用替代能源。他说，未来数周，一些州府雇员也将把车辆送来改装，但须经过技术评估，以确定车辆是否适用。Fashedemi先生说，该倡议旨在表明政府愿意以身作则，而不是仅仅倡议使用替代燃料。他敦促私人投资者把握压缩天然气市场中的机遇，并指出，政府通过基础设施合作给予的支持能够加快加气设施的扩建。与此同时，Rolling Energy Limited首席执行官Mubarak Danbatta称，该项目是政府与私人投资者协作所带来惠益的实例。Danbatta先生赞扬州府提供废弃设施用于重新开发，并表示双方的合作证明，政府可以通过提供现有基础设施的使用机会来促进私人投资。他说：“你们在这里看到的是合作的力量。当私人实体与政府携手合作时，就会产生这样的成果。”他解释说，这座被称为综合加气单元的设施将加气机和压缩机整合在同一套系统中，采用双枪嘴加气机，车辆可从两侧同时加气。据他介绍，这座加气站每天可为约150辆汽车提供服务，具体取决于气瓶容量和压力。其车辆改装中心预计每天也可改装约12辆汽车。随着压缩天然气基础设施投资不断增长，尼日利亚正寻求实现能源结构多元化并降低对汽油的依赖，尤其是在2023年5月取消燃油补贴之后。Tinubu领导的政府多次表示，采用压缩天然气技术是政府推进一系列改革、减轻尼日利亚民众生活成本压力的整体努力的一部分

https://leadership.ng/despite-stiff-chal.title: Despite Stiff Challenge, South East Still Pull Behind Peter Obi
https://leadership.ng/despite-stiff-chal.summary: Findings by LEADERSHIP Weekend across Enugu, Imo, Abia and Anambra states indicate that Peter Obi continues to enjoy considerable political influence in the South-East, particularly among young people, traders and residents dissatisfied with the country’s economic situation. During the meeting, Obi criticised the administration of President Bola Tinubu, arguing that the South-East had not received adequate attention from the Federal Government.
https://leadership.ng/despite-stiff-chal.summary_zh: 《LEADERSHIP》周末在埃努古、伊莫、阿比亚和安帕拉各州开展的调查显示，彼得·奥比在东南部仍享有相当大的政治影响力，尤其是在年轻人、商贩以及对该国经济状况感到不满的居民中间。会上，奥比批评了总统博拉·蒂努布政府，认为联邦政府未能给予东南部充分关注。
https://leadership.ng/despite-stiff-chal.body: Findings by LEADERSHIP Weekend across Enugu, Imo, Abia and Anambra states indicate that Peter Obi continues to enjoy considerable political influence in the South-East, particularly among young people, traders and residents dissatisfied with the country’s economic situation. However, while his supporters are optimistic that he could secure overwhelming votes across the region, some political stakeholders have cautioned that popularity alone may not translate into electoral victory, especially in the face of competing political interests, party structures and concerns about the credibility of the electoral process. In Enugu, investigations by our correspondent revealed that Obi’s influence remains considerably strong, with many residents expressing confidence in his chances of defeating other presidential contenders in the state. Interviews conducted in different parts of the state showed that several residents had already indicated their intention to vote for him in the January 2027 presidential election. His level of acceptability, it was gathered, has remained high since the 2023 general election, with his name becoming familiar across different communities and social groups in the state. A former governorship candidate in Enugu State, Prince Uche Agbo, told LEADERSHIP Weekend that Obi enjoys widespread acceptance and could defeat other presidential candidates by a wide margin. “I don’t want to mention names, but all I know is that Obi is too popular in Enugu State and pulls surprises as usual. He has a better chance of winning than other candidates,” he said. Similarly, a political scientist, Mr Ignatius Mbaeri, rated Obi’s political influence highly, arguing that his growing popularity gives him an advantage over other presidential contenders. “My brother, honestly, the fear of Obi appears to be everywhere. He pulls crowds each time he comes to Enugu, and so he has a better chance of defeating other presidential candidates,” he said. In Imo State, Obi’s political appeal has also been described as phenomenal, with supporters expressing confidence in his capacity to address the country’s economic challenges. Since his emergence as a major presidential contender in 2023, his followership in the state has reportedly continued to grow, driven largely by his promises of economic recovery, prudent management of public resources and investment in critical sectors. A political analyst, Uche Onwuchekwe, told LEADERSHIP Weekend that Nigeria needed a technocrat with the capacity to translate policy ideas into practical solutions. He identified insecurity, healthcare and infrastructure as some of the critical areas requiring urgent attention. “We have overgrown this stage of trial and error. What we need now is a man with the capability to translate words into action,” he said. Onwuchekwe argued that the prevailing economic difficulties had made Nigerians more conscious of the need to elect a president capable of transforming the country. He also suggested that some residents who support Obi might be reluctant to openly declare their political preferences for fear of victimisation. Obi’s recent visit to Imo State further demonstrated the enthusiasm among his supporters. The presidential candidate, who arrived in Owerri from Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, as part of his nationwide town hall series, visited a popular market where he interacted with traders, some of whom presented him with gifts. His subsequent town hall meeting, attended by town union leaders from the 27 local government areas, market women, students, NDC candidates and Obidient Movement organisers, attracted considerable enthusiasm. During the meeting, Obi criticised the administration of President Bola Tinubu, arguing that the South-East had not received adequate attention from the Federal Government. He also raised concerns about insecurity, poverty and the state of the economy, while promising that an NDC administration would prioritise national unity, security, healthcare, education and poverty reduction. Participants also raised concerns about the protection of their votes in 2027, to which Obi assured them that his party would work to ensure that votes counted. However, not all political stakeholders in Imo State believe his growing popularity constitutes a threat to their political interests. The Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the state, Onwuasanya FCC Jones, dismissed suggestions that Obi posed a threat to the party, saying it had already mapped out strategies to win the election. He maintained that Imo voters would support APC candidates, including President Bola Tinubu. Similarly, an NDC stakeholder, Hon. Udubueze Uwaezuoke, said the party was determined to win the presidential election and consolidate its presence across the South-East. Meanwhile, an APGA executive, Dr George Nworji, said his party had adopted President Tinubu as its presidential candidate and would work towards delivering him in the region through grassroots mobilisation. In Abia State, findings indicate that Obi’s political influence remains strong despite his yet-to-be-reported campaign visit to the state since the flag-off of his presidential campaign activities. According to our correspondent, his supporters appear eager to receive him, with his popularity being driven largely by youths and residents dissatisfied with the prevailing economic situation. Reliable findings indicated that even some members of other political parties in the state had made up their minds to vote for Obi for president while supporting their respective parties’ candidates for other elective positions. The support, it was gathered, is influenced by ethnic considerations, political expectations, economic concerns, his persistent criticism of the Tinubu administration and his perceived commitment to transparency and prudent management of public funds. In Anambra State, however, reactions to the chances of Obi and his running mate, former Kano State Governor, Alhaji Rabiu Kwankwaso, have been mixed, although many respondents expressed confidence in the ticket. With about 72 days to the January 16, 2027 general election, political party leaders, analysts, business operators and ordinary voters who spoke to LEADERSHIP Weekend agreed that the performance of the APC-led Federal Government could work against President Tinubu’s re-election. They, however, expressed concerns that electoral manipulation, vote-buying and the influence of political structures could affect the outcome. The Senator representing Anambra Central Senatorial District, Senator Victor Umeh, expressed confidence that Obi and Kwankwaso would secure overwhelming support, predicting that the ticket could win more than 70 per cent of the votes nationwide. Similarly, the NDC Chairman in Anambra State, Hon. Ikem Uzoezie, and the State Coordinator of the party’s Presidential Campaign Council, Hon. Ifeanyi Ibezi, expressed optimism that Obi would record between 70 and 95 per cent of the votes in the state. Uzoezie recalled that Obi polled more than 500,000 votes in Anambra during the 2023 presidential election as the Labour Party candidate, expressing confidence that he could secure at least 1.5 million votes in the state in 2027. Umeh argued that Obi had demonstrated his political strength in 2023 despite lacking the political structures enjoyed by established political parties. He also said the NDC was making arrangements to protect its votes, including plans to deploy three party agents to each polling unit nationwide. A lawyer and public affairs analyst, Mr Maxwell Ezeude, also expressed optimism about Obi’s chances, citing his alliance with Kwankwaso and the prevailing economic hardship. He argued that the alliance had strengthened Obi’s political prospects by giving him access to a wider political constituency, particularly in the North. However, Ezeude warned that the influence of money in Nigerian politics, the alignment of state governors with the ruling party and possible electoral manipulation could constitute major obstacles. A community leader, Mr Tony Okafor, predicted that Obi could win overwhelmingly in the South-East and secure significant support nationally if the election was free and fair. He said many Nigerians were looking for a leader who could reduce the cost of governance and redirect public resources towards improving their welfare. The factional Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Anambra State, Comrade Patrick Obianyo, said winning the 2027 presidential election would be difficult for Obi because his political strength was now better understood by his opponents. He argued that vote-buying, financial inducements and the influence of state governors could affect the outcome. Similarly, a media consultant, Mr Titus Eleweke, acknowledged that Obi could secure considerable votes in the South-East but expressed doubts about his ability to replicate the same level of support in the North. Other respondents, however, maintained that the prevailing economic hardship could influence voters to reject the ruling party. A real estate operator, Mr Ekene Thomas, expressed confidence that young people would resist attempts to manipulate the election, while a bar attendant, Miss Uchechukwu Chukwubuike, said she would vote for Obi because of the economic difficulties confronting Nigerians. Across the four states, the findings suggest that Obi continues to enjoy considerable goodwill, with his political appeal extending beyond party membership and attracting residents who believe that the country needs a change in leadership. Nevertheless, the extent to which this enthusiasm will translate into actual votes remains a major question. While his popularity appears particularly strong in Anambra, his home state, and extends to Enugu, Imo and Abia, the positions of APGA, APC and other political stakeholders demonstrate that the South-East is not without competing political interests. The January 16, 2027 presidential election will therefore provide a clearer test of whether Obi can convert his grassroots appeal, political alliances and growing support base into electoral support across the South-East. For now, the findings point to sustained political enthusiasm around Obi in the four states covered by this investigation, although the absence of findings from Ebonyi means the assessment does not yet represent the entire South-East region. https://leadership.ng/despite-stiff-chal.title_zh: 尽管面临严峻挑战，东南部地区仍落后于Peter Obi
https://leadership.ng/despite-stiff-chal.body_zh:
LEADERSHIP Weekend在埃努古、伊莫、阿比亚和安ambara州开展的调查显示，Peter Obi在尼日利亚东南部 continues to enjoy considerable political influence，特别是在年轻人、贸易商以及不满该国经济状况的居民中。然而，尽管其支持者乐观认为他可能在整个地区获得压倒性选票，一些政治利益相关者警告说，人气本身未必能转化为选举胜利，尤其是在 competing political interests、党务组织结构以及对选举进程可信度存在担忧的情况下。

在埃努古州，本报驻记者调查显示，Obi的影响力依然相当强劲，许多居民相信他有望击败该州其他总统竞选人。在该州不同地区进行的采访显示，数名居民已表示打算在2027年1月总统选举中投票给他。采访汇总情况显示，自2023年大选以来，他的支持率一直保持高位，他的名字已为该州不同社区和社会群体所熟知。埃努古州前州长候选人Prince Uche Agbo告诉LEADERSHIP Weekend，Obi在埃努古州广受欢迎，能够以较大优势击败其他总统候选人。他说：“我不想点名，但我知道Obi在埃努古州太受欢迎了，而且他一如既往地总能带来惊喜。他获胜的机会比其他候选人都大。”

同样，政治学学者Ignatius Mbaeri先生高度评价Obi的政治影响力，认为他日益增长的人气使他相较其他总统竞选人占据优势。他说：“兄弟，坦白说，对Obi的恐惧似乎无处不在。他每次来到埃努古都能吸引大批人群，因此他击败其他总统候选人的机会更大。”

在伊莫州，Obi的政治吸引力也被形容为非同寻常，支持者相信他有能力应对该国面临的经济挑战。自2023年成为主要总统竞选人以来，据报道他在该州的追随者持续增加，这主要得益于他关于经济复苏、公共资源审慎管理和投资关键领域的承诺。政治分析师Uche Onwuchekwe告诉LEADERSHIP Weekend，尼日利亚需要一位能够将政策理念转化为切实解决方案的技术型领导人。他指出，安全局势、医疗保健和基础设施是一些亟须关注的关键领域。他说：“我们已经过度依赖这个试错阶段。现在我们需要的是一个能够把言语转化为行动的人。”Onwuchekwe认为，当前的经济困境已使尼日利亚人更加清醒地认识到，需要选出一位有能力改变国家面貌的总统。他还暗示，一些支持Obi的居民可能因为害怕遭到迫害，而不愿公开表明政治立场。

Obi最近访问伊莫州进一步显示其支持者的热情。这位总统竞选人从巴耶尔萨州叶纳戈阿抵达奥韦里，作为全国市政厅系列活动的一部分，他走访了一座热门市场并与贸易商交流，其中一些人还向他赠送了礼物。随后举行的市政厅会议有27个地方政府区域的城镇协会领袖、市场妇女、学生、NDC候选人和Obidient Movement组织者参加，现场气氛热烈。会议期间，Obi批评总统Bola Tinubu政府，认为联邦政府没有给予东南部足够关注。他还提出了对安全、贫困和经济状况的担忧，同时承诺NDC执政后将优先关注国家团结、安全、医疗保健、教育和减贫。与会者还提出关切，要求保障他们在2027年的选票得到保护，Obi向他们保证，他的党将努力确保选票得到计入。

然而，伊莫州并非所有政治利益相关者都认为他日益增长的人气对自己的政治利益构成威胁。全进步大会党（APC）州宣传秘书Onwuasanya FCC Jones否定了Obi对该党构成威胁的说法，称该党已经制定winning strategies to win the election。他坚持认为，伊莫州选民将支持APC候选人，包括总统Bola Tinubu。同样，NDC利益相关者Udubueze Uwaezuoke阁下表示，该党决心赢得总统选举，并巩固其在东南部的存在。与此同时，APGA执行委员George Nworji博士说，该党已采纳总统Tinubu作为总统候选人，并将通过基层动员在该地区推动他胜选。

在阿比亚州，调查显示，尽管Obi的总统竞选活动启动以来尚未访问该州，但他的政治影响力依然强劲。据本报驻记者称，他的支持者似乎热切期待他的到来，而他的人气主要由年轻人和不满当前经济状况的居民推动。可靠调查显示，该州甚至一些其他政党的成员也已决定在其他公职选举中支持本党候选人的同时，投票支持Obi竞选总统。据汇总情况，这种支持受到族群因素、政治期待、经济担忧、他对Tinubu政府持续不断的批评，以及外界认为他致力于透明和公共资金审慎管理等因素的影响。

然而，在安ambara州，对于Obi及其竞选搭档、前卡诺州州长Alhaji Rabiu Kwankwaso胜选前景的反应不一，尽管许多受访者对二人的组合表示有信心。距离2027年1月16日大选约72天，接受LEADERSHIP Weekend采访的各政党领袖、分析人士、商业经营者和普通选民一致认为，APC主导的联邦政府的表现可能对总统Tinubu连任不利。不过，他们也担忧选举操弄、买票和政党组织结构的影响可能左右结果。

代表安amb拉中部选区的参议员Victor Umeh参议员对Obi和Kwankwaso能否获得压倒性支持表示有信心，预测这套候选人组合可能在全国赢得超过70%的选票。同样，安ambara州NDC主席Ikem Uzoezie阁下及该党总统竞选委员会州协调员Ifeanyi Ibezi阁下乐观表示，Obi将在该州获得70%至95%的选票。Uzoezie回忆称，Obi在2023年总统选举中以工党候选人身份参选，在安amb拉获得了超过500,000票，并相信他2027年能在该州赢得至少150万票。Umeh认为，尽管缺乏成熟政党所具备的政党组织结构，Obi在2023年已经证明了其政治实力。他还说，NDC正在制定保护本党选票的措施，包括计划在全国每个投票站部署3名政党监票员。

律师兼公共事务分析师Maxwell Ezeude先生也对Obi的胜选前景表示乐观，并提到他与Kwankwaso结盟以及当前的经济困境。他认为，这一联盟让Obi得以接触更广泛的政治群体，尤其是在北部地区，从而增强了他的政治胜算。然而，Ezeude警告称，金钱在尼日利亚政治中的影响、州长与执政党的结盟以及潜在的选举操弄，都可能构成重大障碍。社区领袖Tony Okafor先生预测，如果选举自由、公平，Obi可以在东南部以压倒性优势获胜，并在全国获得大量支持。他说，许多尼日利亚人正在寻找一位能够降低治理成本、把公共资源转用于改善民生福祉的领导人。安ambara州非洲民主大会（ADC）派系主席Patrick Obianyo同志说，Obi赢得2027年总统选举并不容易，因为其政治实力如今已得到对手更充分的了解。他认为，买票、经济诱因和州长的影响都可能左右结果。同样，媒体顾问Titus Eleweke先生承认Obi可以在东南部获得相当多的选票，但怀疑他能否在北部复制同等水平的支持。

不过，其他受访者坚持认为，当前经济困境可能促使选民拒绝执政党。房地产经营者Ekene Thomas先生相信年轻人会抵制操纵选举的企图；酒吧服务员Uchechukwu Chukwubuike小姐则表示，由于尼日利亚人正面临经济困难，她将投票给Obi。

在这四个州的调查结果表明，Obi continues to enjoy considerable goodwill，其政治吸引力超出了党派成员范围，吸引了认为国家需要领导层变革的居民。然而，这份热情最终能在多大程度上转化为实际选票，仍是一个重大问题。尽管他的人气似乎在其家乡安ambara州尤为强劲，并延伸至埃努古、伊莫和阿比亚，但APGA、APC及其他政治利益相关者的立场表明，东南部并非不存在相互竞争的政治利益。因此，2027年1月16日总统选举将更清楚地检验Obi能否将其基层号召力、政治联盟和不断扩大的支持基础转化为整个东南部的选举支持。目前，调查结果显示，在本次调查覆盖的四个州，围绕Obi的政治热情持续不减；不过，由于没有获得埃博尼州的调查结果，这项评估尚不能代表整个东南部地区。

https://leadership.ng/abba-aji-clarifies.body: The retired Justice said the travel ban to the United States was still subsisting against the justices. Justice Abba Aji who spoke on the occasion of a valedictory Supreme Court session held in her honour, however, noted that the ban was part of inconveniences and a small price to pay by judicial officers to preserve the chastity of justice. Abba Aji is to formally bow out of the Supreme Court on November 7 upon attainment of the mandatory retirement age of 70 years. Recalling her experience while on the bench, she said, “My time on the Supreme Court bench was filled with challenges, some of which have served as additional opportunities to stand firm on the side of justice, regardless of the consequences. Although, Justice Abba Aji did not disclose the judgment that attracted the US travel ban on her panel members, she however said, “Such inconveniences were a price to pay to preserve the chastity of justice”. Justice Abba Aji also recalled the year 2016 while on a programme at Washington DC in the USA, she received a call that her attention was needed by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) over a petition against her in Lagos. She explained that the petition made her a regular visitor at the EFCC office answering questions on allegations of corruption she knew nothing about adding that, at the end of the investigations, she was exonerated from all the allegations. Despite the exoneration, she said the situation was chaotic and made a very difficult time for her as slanders had filled the air, adding that to worsen the situation, she could not speak in her own defense in public because of the conservative nature of the judiciary. The retiring apex court justice, charged younger generation of judges to hold fast to integrity and let justice be their compass. She counseled serving judges to serve with humility and courage and to always remember that the law is not merely a profession but a trust. Earlier, the Chief Justice of Nigeria CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, who presided over the special court session congratulated Justice Abba Aji for diligent service to the country’s judiciary and for leaving the Supreme Court bench with unblemished record of service. https://leadership.ng/abba-aji-clarifies.title_zh: 阿巴·阿吉澄清美国针对最高法院大法官的旅行禁令
https://leadership.ng/abba-aji-clarifies.body_zh: 已退休的大法官表示，针对法官的美国旅行禁令仍然有效。在为表彰她而举行的最高法院告别会议上发言的Abba Aji大法官指出，这项禁令虽会带来不便，却只是司法人员为维护司法廉洁所付出的微小代价。Abba Aji大法官将在达到70岁的强制退休年龄后，于11月7日正式退出最高法院。回顾自己担任法官期间的经历，她说：“我在最高法院任职期间充满了挑战，其中一些挑战也给我提供了额外机会，让我无论面对何种后果都能坚定不移地站在正义一边。”尽管Abba Aji大法官没有透露导致她及合议庭其他成员受到美国旅行禁令的具体判决，但她表示：“这种不便是为维护司法廉洁而必须付出的代价。”Abba Aji大法官还回忆说，2016年，她在美国华盛顿特区参加一个项目期间，接到经济和金融犯罪委员会（EFCC）的电话，要求她到拉各斯就针对她的申诉接受问询。她解释说，这项申诉使她经常前往经济和金融犯罪委员会办公室，回答有关她毫不知情的腐败指控；调查结束后，她洗清了所有指控。尽管最终洗清嫌疑，她表示当时的局面十分混乱，令她的日子非常艰难，因为诽谤之声四处弥漫；更糟的是，由于司法界作风保守，她无法在公开场合为自己辩护。这位即将退休的最高法院大法官告诫年轻一代法官，要坚守正直，以正义作为行动指南。她劝勉在职法官以谦逊和勇气履职，并始终牢记，法律不仅是一门职业，更是一项责任。此前，主持特别法院会议的尼日利亚首席大法官（CJN）Kudirat Kekere-Ekun大法官祝贺Abba Aji大法官为该国司法界勤勉履职，并Cleanly完成了最高法院法官任期。CJN表示，Abba Aji大法官在司法界和法律界的职业生涯，对国家以及所有以她为榜样进入法官行列的女性而言都具有重大意义。我们掌握独家优势。获取实时报道、突发新闻和独家视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp频道，全天候获取最新消息 → 加入我们的WhatsApp频道 --> --> Olakunle Olasanmi Olakunle Olasanmi是《LEADERSHIP Newspaper》的记者，拥有20多年经验，专长于司法报道。在其职业生涯中，他在报道尼日利亚及其他地区的司法体系和冲突解决方面表现卓越。通过准确、生动和独家的报道，他已成为法律事务领域值得信赖的权威。
